preview.headline: Senators Bring Possession Edge Into Winnipeg to Face Streaking Jets
preview.summary: An in-form Ottawa Senators squad boasting strong play-play metrics travels to face a Winnipeg Jets team riding a six-game winning streak on two days of rest.
preview.away_analysis: The Senators control play effectively, ranking 3rd in Corsi For% at 53.8 and driving high shot-attempt volume through strong offensive-zone pressure. They back up those underlying numbers with elite finishing, supported by Ullmark's stellar goaltending performance ranking 5th in GSAx over his last 20 games. However, special teams represent a glaring weak spot, anchored by an abysmal 11.54% power play that ranks dead last in the league.
preview.home_analysis: The Jets enter on a six-game win streak despite middling underlying metrics, ranking 22nd in Corsi For% and 21st in expected goals share. They keep games tight by limiting chances defensively, ranking 7th in expected goals against per 60, but struggle to generate sustained offense at 5-on-5. Special teams present a mixed bag with a capable 24.24% power play offsetting a leaky penalty kill operating at just 72.13%.
matchup_edges: Ottawa holds a massive territorial advantage at 5-on-5, outranking Winnipeg significantly in Corsi For% and shot-generation volume.
The Senators feature a top-tier goaltending edge with Ullmark ranking 5th in recent GSAx compared to Skinner at 50th.
Winnipeg boasts a substantial special-teams edge on the power play, ranking 12th against Ottawa's league-worst 32nd-ranked unit.
preview.x_factor: Goaltending disparity, as Ullmark's elite recent form for Ottawa clashes with Skinner's struggles to provide stable defensive rescue for Winnipeg.
preview.key_question: Can the Jets leverage their lethal power play and opportunistic winning streak to mask a severe 5-on-5 possession deficit against a dominant Senators team?
preview.quick_takeaway: Ottawa's dominant territorial control and elite goaltending clash with Winnipeg's surging win streak and special-teams upside.

preview.headline: Bruins Hold Edge in High‑Danger Matchup vs Kings
preview.summary: The Boston Bruins’ superior high‑danger chance generation and better expected‑goals profile give them a clear statistical edge, while the Kings’ recent struggles and weaker penalty‑kill leave them vulnerable. Both teams are evenly rested, but the Bruins’ stronger goaltending and offensive efficiency should tip the scales.
preview.away_analysis: The Kings’ 49.82% Corsi For and 51.22% Goals For place them mid‑league, but their 48.79% Expected Goals and 18th‑ranked shooting suggest finishing woes. Their 21.67% power‑play is respectable, yet a 29th‑ranked penalty‑kill and 4.17 penalties per 60 undermine their advantage. The recent four‑game losing streak and 2‑day rest hint at fatigue, while goalie Kuemper’s 75th‑ranked GSAx indicates a sub‑average last‑20 performance.
preview.home_analysis: Boston’s 50.93% Corsi For and 58.33% Goals For rank them in the top tier, while a 54.54% Expected Goals and 3rd‑ranked high‑danger chances show they’re generating quality shots. Their 11.67% shooting is elite, and a 80.28% penalty‑kill (11th) keeps opponents from capitalizing on penalties. Despite a 2‑day rest and a two‑game losing streak, goalie Swayman’s 11th‑ranked GSAx signals solid recent form.
matchup_edges: Boston’s 57.55% high‑danger chances versus LA’s 51.84% give the Bruins a 6‑point advantage in quality shot generation
Boston’s 3rd‑ranked xGF/60 (3.1) outpaces LA’s 12th (2.83), underscoring offensive efficiency
Boston’s 11th‑ranked GSAx vs LA’s 75th shows a goalie advantage for the Bruins
preview.x_factor: The Kings’ recent four‑game slide and weaker penalty‑kill create a psychological and tactical disadvantage that Boston can exploit, especially given the Bruins’ superior high‑danger production.
preview.key_question: Will the Kings’ power‑play success offset their sub‑average expected goals and penalty‑kill weaknesses, or will Boston’s high‑danger dominance and better goaltending seal the game?
preview.quick_takeaway: Boston’s high‑danger edge and better goaltending give them a slight but meaningful advantage over the Kings’ struggling offense and weak penalty kill.

preview.headline: Islanders' Power‑Play Edge vs Blue Jackets' Discipline Clash
preview.summary: The New York Islanders, riding a two‑game win streak, will host the Columbus Blue Jackets, who are on a four‑game slide. While the Islanders generate more expected goals and boast a higher shooting percentage, the Blue Jackets’ elite penalty‑kill and disciplined play could keep the game tight. The matchup pivots on whether the Islanders can convert their high‑danger chances into goals and if the Blue Jackets’ defensive discipline will neutralize the Islanders’ offensive firepower.
preview.away_analysis: Columbus’ possession numbers are solid—Corsi % at 50.78 (rank 13) and Corsi / 60 at 55.17 (rank 19)—but their shooting efficiency is low, with a 6.85 % rate (31st). They out‑shoot the Islanders in high‑danger chances (45.75 % vs 48.78 %) yet their expected goals for per 60 (2.4) lag behind New York’s 2.91. The Blue Jackets’ penalty‑kill is a bright spot, 73.47 % (23rd), and their penalties taken per 60 (3.34) rank 5th, indicating disciplined play that could keep the game close. Talbot’s recent GSAx rank of 12 suggests he’s been solid over the last 20 games.
preview.home_analysis: New York is firing on all cylinders: a 49.02 % goals‑for rate (13th) and a 10.46 % shooting percentage (9th). Their expected goals for per 60 (2.91) rank 7th, and they generate high‑danger chances at 48.78 % (20th). Despite a weaker penalty kill (85.94 %—4th), the Islanders’ power play (17.24 %) is decent. Sorokin’s GSAx rank of 7 signals strong recent performance. The Islanders’ Corsi % of 47.02 (28th) suggests they’re being out‑possessed, but they compensate with a higher shot‑attempt quality.
matchup_edges: Islanders’ high‑danger generation and shooting edge may outpace the Blue Jackets’ defensive discipline
Blue Jackets’ penalty‑kill prowess and disciplined play can blunt the Islanders’ offensive output
The Blue Jackets’ low shooting efficiency could keep the score tight if the Islanders fail to convert
preview.x_factor: If the Islanders’ high‑danger chances translate into goals, they’ll likely pull ahead; otherwise, the Blue Jackets’ disciplined, penalty‑kill heavy game could keep the score close.
preview.key_question: Will the Islanders’ superior shooting and high‑danger chances overcome the Blue Jackets’ disciplined defense and penalty‑kill strength?
preview.quick_takeaway: The game hinges on whether the Islanders can turn their high‑danger chances into goals, while the Blue Jackets’ disciplined play and strong penalty kill keep the score tight.

preview.headline: Oilers’ Power‑Play Fire vs Panthers’ Defensive Resilience
preview.summary: The Edmonton Oilers, riding a five‑game streak, will test their high‑percentage power play against the Tampa Bay Panthers’ top‑ranked penalty kill. Both teams are evenly matched in rest and schedule density, but Edmonton’s 34.25% PP contrasts sharply with Tampa Bay’s 85.88% PK, while the Panthers’ possession edge (Corsi For % 50.84 vs. 47.5) suggests they can control the flow of the game.
preview.away_analysis: Edmonton’s 34.25% power‑play rate, a league‑ranked 2nd best, is a clear weapon that can swing momentum, especially against a Panthers squad that has struggled to capitalize on their own opportunities (GF % 41.67). The Oilers’ Corsi For % of 47.5, however, ranks 26th, indicating they may have to rely more on special‑teams play than on sustaining possession. Their shooting percentage (7.91%) is solid, but their expected‑goals percentage (43.82%) lags, hinting at a finishing gap that could be exploited by a disciplined defense.
preview.home_analysis: Tampa Bay’s 50.84% Corsi For % places them 12th in the league, giving them a possession advantage that can limit Edmonton’s shots. Their penalty‑kill prowess (85.88%) is among the best, and their expected‑goals‑against per 60 (2.48) is the 7th best, underscoring a stingy defense that will force Edmonton to generate high‑danger chances. The Panthers’ own power play (24.72%) is respectable, but their shooting percentage (7.81%) is slightly lower, suggesting they may struggle to convert when Edmonton’s defense is on the back foot.
matchup_edges: Edmonton’s elite power play vs. Tampa Bay’s top‑tier penalty kill
Tampa Bay’s possession edge (Corsi For %) gives them a flow advantage
Edmonton’s higher shooting percentage could offset their lower expected‑goals output
preview.x_factor: Will Edmonton’s power‑play explosions overcome a Panthers’ disciplined defense that thrives on limiting high‑danger chances?
preview.key_question: Can Edmonton’s special‑teams strength compensate for their lower possession numbers against a Panthers squad that dominates in Corsi and kills penalties at an elite rate?
preview.quick_takeaway: Edmonton’s power‑play prowess is the matchup’s biggest edge, but Tampa Bay’s possession control and penalty‑kill depth could keep the game tight.

preview.headline: Flyers’ High‑Danger Edge vs Sabres’ Corsi Advantage
preview.summary: The Flyers’ 5th‑ranked HDCF% and 4th‑ranked xGF% give them a clear edge in creating and finishing chances, while the Sabres’ 7th‑ranked Corsi For % and 8th‑ranked CF/60 show they control the puck. Both teams are on losing streaks and have similar recent workloads, so the matchup will hinge on how well each can convert their possession advantage into goals.
preview.away_analysis: The Sabres dominate possession—53% Corsi and 58.3 CF/60—yet their shooting at 8.12% is the league’s 23rd best. They’re also struggling on the power play (14.7%) and have a weak penalty kill (70.4%). Their recent L4 streak and 2‑day rest could sap the energy needed to finish their chances.
preview.home_analysis: The Flyers generate the most dangerous chances (56.85%) and boast the league’s 4th‑ranked expected goals. Their shooting is solid at 8.86% and their penalty kill (77.8%) is the 17th best. A one‑day rest after two games in four days keeps them sharp, but the lone loss might hurt confidence.
matchup_edges: Flyers’ high‑danger production is 7.8% higher than the Sabres’ HDCF%
Sabres’ 53% Corsi For % outpaces the Flyers’ 50.4%
Flyers’ penalty‑kill edge of 7.4% could swing late‑game power‑play opportunities
preview.x_factor: Flyers’ ability to convert high‑danger chances into goals may offset the Sabres’ puck control, but the Sabres’ disciplined defense and higher CF/60 could keep the game tight.
preview.key_question: Will the Flyers’ higher expected‑goal output translate into a win despite their weaker power‑play percentage, or will the Sabres’ puck possession and defensive structure hold the Flyers to a low‑scoring affair?
preview.quick_takeaway: Flyers’ dangerous chance creation versus Sabres’ possession control will decide the game; the outcome hinges on who converts better.

preview.headline: Maple Leafs’ Power‑Play Edge vs. Blackhawks’ Defensive Resilience
preview.summary: Toronto’s sixth straight loss has left the Leafs struggling to generate offense, but their elite power‑play and penalty‑kill rates give them a tactical advantage over Chicago, whose own special‑teams performance is middling. The matchup hinges on whether the Leafs can convert high‑danger chances into goals while the Blackhawks can suppress the Leafs’ chances and capitalize on their own power‑play opportunities.
preview.away_analysis: The Leafs sit in the middle of the pack on possession (Corsi 49.2, rank 21) and have a solid high‑danger chance share (51.05 %, rank 16). Their power‑play efficiency (26.67 %, rank 6) and penalty‑kill (85.71 %, rank 7) are among the league’s best, giving them a strong special‑teams advantage. However, their recent six‑game losing streak and only 2 rest days signal fatigue that could blunt their offensive output.
preview.home_analysis: Chicago’s stats show a defensive focus: Corsi 45.78 (rank 31) and goals‑for 35.42 % (rank 32) reflect limited offensive production, but they keep opponents’ expected goals low (xGA/60 2.77, rank 21). Their penalty kill (78.12 %, rank 16) is respectable, yet their power‑play (14.29 %, rank 30) is a liability. The Blackhawks’ recent two games in the past week and 2 rest days mirror Toronto’s schedule, keeping the fatigue factor equal.
matchup_edges: Toronto’s elite power‑play (rank 6) could offset Chicago’s poor PP (rank 30)
Chicago’s defensive discipline (xGA/60 rank 21) may suppress Toronto’s high‑danger chances
Both teams have similar rest and recent workload, making special‑teams the key differentiator
preview.x_factor: Toronto’s ability to finish high‑danger chances will be tested against Chicago’s disciplined penalty‑kill and defensive structure; if the Leafs can convert, their power‑play edge may be decisive.
preview.key_question: Can the Maple Leafs’ power‑play and penalty‑kill prowess overcome the Blackhawks’ defensive suppression and limited offensive upside?
preview.quick_takeaway: Toronto’s special‑teams advantage could swing the game, but Chicago’s defensive focus may neutralize the Leafs’ high‑danger chances.

preview.headline: Capitals Visit Lightning in Battle of Possession-Heavy Contenders
preview.summary: The Washington Capitals travel to face the Tampa Bay Lightning on November 17, 2026, in a matchup of two elite possession teams looking to bounce back from recent losing streaks. Both squads enter with two days of rest after playing three games in the last week, setting the stage for a sharp tactical battle.
preview.away_analysis: The Capitals control play effectively, ranking 2nd in Corsi For % and 3rd in Corsi For per 60, while holding a strong 7th-place standing in Expected Goals %. However, their 14th-ranked Goals For % sits below their underlying chance generation of 2.98 expected goals per 60, pointing to some minor finishing friction. Thompson anchors the crease behind a defensive structure that surrenders 2.53 expected goals against per 60, though special teams remain an area for improvement with bottom-tier rankings on both the power play and penalty kill.
preview.home_analysis: The Lightning mirror Washington's territorial dominance, ranking 4th in Corsi For % and 6th in Expected Goals %. Unlike the Capitals, Tampa Bay capitalizes ruthlessly on chances, boasting the league's top shooting percentage and a 5th-ranked Goals For %. Vasilevskiy will look to stabilize the backend for a team that suppresses chances well, ranking 5th in expected goals against per 60, despite a struggling penalty kill that sits 25th in the league.
matchup_edges: Washington holds a slight edge in volume generation, ranking 2nd in Corsi For % compared to Tampa Bay's 4th.
Tampa Bay features elite finishing power, leading the NHL in shooting percentage while Washington ranks 10th.
Tampa Bay displays better defensive suppression, ranking 5th in expected goals against per 60 compared to Washington's 11th.
preview.x_factor: Special teams discipline will be critical, as both clubs struggle on the penalty kill and must avoid giving high-end power plays unnecessary opportunities.
preview.key_question: Can Washington's high-volume shot generation finally break through against Tampa Bay's elite finishing and goaltending?
preview.quick_takeaway: This is a clash of elite play-driving metrics where Tampa Bay's lethal finishing efficiency meets Washington's high-volume possession attack.

preview.headline: Wild Host Fatigued Predators in Central Division Clash
preview.summary: The Minnesota Wild return home on a three-game winning streak to face a Nashville Predators squad playing their fourth game in seven days. Minnesota won the first meeting 3-1 back on October 1st.
preview.away_analysis: The Predators arrive under heavy schedule pressure, playing their fourth game in seven days with just one day of rest. While they struggle to suppress shot attempts ranking 30th in Corsi Against per 60, they excel on special teams with the league's top penalty kill at 90.0% and a strong power play ranking 7th. Juuse Saros anchors the back end, holding the 4th-best GSAx rank over his last 20 games.
preview.home_analysis: The Wild enter well-rested with two days off and a three-game winning streak, boasting a blistering 71.11% goals-for percentage that ranks 2nd in the league. Minnesota controls play effectively with above-average expected goals and high-danger chance shares while converting at a sharp 10.7% shooting clip. Jesper Wallstedt boosts their defense, coming in with the number one GSAx ranking over his last 20 games.
matchup_edges: Nashville holds a massive special teams advantage on the penalty kill, ranking 1st in the league compared to Minnesota's 14th-ranked unit.
Minnesota carries a significant rest advantage, playing their first game in three days while Nashville plays their fourth game in a compressed seven-day span.
The Wild boast elite finishing and goaltending form, backed by Jesper Wallstedt's top-ranked recent GSAx and a top-10 shooting percentage.
preview.x_factor: Fatigue vs. Form: Can Nashville's top-ranked penalty kill and Juuse Saros weather the storm against a well-rested Wild team riding a three-game winning streak?
preview.key_question: Will the Predators' heavy recent workload catch up to them defensively against Minnesota's efficient attack?
preview.quick_takeaway: A well-rested Wild squad with elite goaltending form squares off against a fatigued Predators team relying on special teams and Saros to survive a brutal schedule stretch.

preview.headline: Ducks’ Power‑Play Prowess Meets Blues’ Defensive Discipline
preview.summary: The Ducks will rely on their elite power‑play and high shooting percentage to counter the Blues’ strong defensive play and high‑danger chance generation. Both teams are evenly matched on the ice, but the Ducks’ special‑teams edge and the Blues’ goaltending depth could tip the scales.
preview.away_analysis: Anaheim’s 35.21% PP is the best in the league, and their 11.52% shooting shows they finish well when they get chances. Their Corsi For % sits at 50.29, just above the league median, but their expected‑goals per 60 (2.61) ranks 19th, suggesting they’re generating fewer quality chances than their shot totals imply. The Ducks are also the most penalty‑prone (4.78 per 60), which could keep the Blues’ penalty kill from shining.
preview.home_analysis: St. Louis boasts the 4th‑ranked expected‑goals per 60 (2.98) and a high‑danger chances % of 54.2, indicating they’re creating quality chances at a high rate. Their 84.61% PK is the 8th best, and they take few penalties (2.98 per 60), keeping their penalty kill sharp. However, their shooting percentage of 7.06% is the lowest in the league, hinting at finishing struggles when they get the chances.
matchup_edges: Anaheim’s top‑tier power play could exploit the Blues’ limited penalty kill efficiency
St. Louis’ high‑danger chance generation could offset the Ducks’ lower expected‑goals output
The Blues’ goaltender, ranked 8th in recent GSAx, offers a defensive anchor that could neutralize Anaheim’s shooting burst
preview.x_factor: The game hinges on whether Anaheim’s power‑play can convert against a Blues defense that excels at shutting down high‑danger chances and whose goalie is in elite form.
preview.key_question: Will the Ducks’ special‑teams advantage outweigh the Blues’ defensive discipline and goaltending depth in a tightly contested matchup?
preview.quick_takeaway: Anaheim’s power‑play edge vs. St. Louis’ defensive prowess sets up a classic battle of offense vs. defense.

preview.headline: Stars Look to Extend Roll Against Struggling Golden Knights
preview.summary: The Dallas Stars visit the Vegas Golden Knights on November 17, 2026, bringing a two-game winning streak into a matchup against a Vegas squad searching for answers after dropping two straight. Both teams enter on identical rest with three games played over the last seven days, but their underlying metrics tell vastly different stories.
preview.away_analysis: The Stars are driving play at an elite level, ranking 2nd in Expected Goals % at 59.53% and boasting the league's top-ranked expected goals against rate at 1.92 per 60. While their actual goal conversion has lagged behind their process with a modest 42.86% Goals For %, their elite high-danger chance suppression and Oettinger's solid ninth-ranked GSAx form a formidable foundation. Special teams are also clicking, anchored by a stellar 88.41% penalty kill that ranks 3rd overall.
preview.home_analysis: Vegas enters this contest battling both form and finishing woes, sitting dead last in the league with a 6.59% shooting percentage that has dragged their actual goal share down to 40%. Their underlying numbers are more respectable, sitting 13th in Expected Goals % and featuring a dangerous power play operating at 28.79% efficiency. However, defensive suppression remains a concern with a 76.78% penalty kill and a high volume of defensive-zone pressure allowed.
matchup_edges: Dallas owns a massive expected goal-share advantage, ranking 2nd in xGF% compared to Vegas at 13th.
The Stars boast the league's stingiest defensive suppression, ranking 1st in expected goals against per 60.
Vegas holds a notable special teams edge with their 4th-ranked power play squaring off against Dallas, though the Stars counter with the 3rd-ranked penalty kill.
preview.x_factor: Finishing talent will dictate the pace, as both clubs severely underperform their expected goals due to low shooting percentages.
preview.key_question: Can the Golden Knights generate enough traffic to crack Dallas's top-ranked defensive structure, or will the Stars' possession dominance dictate the game?
preview.quick_takeaway: Dallas controls the territorial and defensive battlegrounds, but Vegas owns the special teams firepower to steal a result if their finishing finally rebounds.

preview.headline: Flames Visit San Jose Looking to Sweep Season Series Against Struggling Sharks
preview.summary: The Calgary Flames travel to face the San Jose Sharks on November 17, 2026, holding a previous 2-1 victory from their November 2 meeting. Both teams enter on identical rest with 1 day off, though the Sharks carry a two-game winning streak into the contest.
preview.away_analysis: The Flames struggle to generate offense, ranking 29th in shooting percentage (7.46%) and 24th in expected goals for per 60 minutes. However, they boast a potent power play that ranks 5th in the league at 27.08% and a solid penalty kill ranking 9th. With Wolf in net, Calgary will look to capitalize on special teams to offset their suppressed 5-on-5 chance generation.
preview.home_analysis: The Sharks face heavy defensive pressure, ranking 32nd in expected goals against per 60 minutes and 31st in Corsi against per 60. Their underlying metrics reflect a struggling possession game, sitting 31st in expected goals percentage (39.88%). Despite these defensive struggles, Askarov provides a stabilizing presence with a strong 21st rank in GSAx over his last 20 games.
matchup_edges: Flames hold a major special teams advantage with the league's 5th-ranked power play against a San Jose penalty kill ranking 21st.
Flames maintain superior defensive suppression, ranking 18th in expected goals against per 60 compared to the Sharks' 32nd ranking.
Sharks possess a notable edge in recent goaltending form, with Askarov ranking 21st in GSAx over his last 20 games.
preview.x_factor: Special teams execution, particularly whether Calgary's 5th-ranked power play can exploit a vulnerable San Jose penalty kill.
preview.key_question: Can the Sharks' defense withstand Calgary's sustained pressure, or will Askarov have to steal another game?
preview.quick_takeaway: Calgary holds the upper hand analytically at 5-on-5 and special teams, but San Jose's recent form and goaltending give them a puncher's chance on home ice.
